rotations.name: Corn - Soybean (your current rotation)
rotations.replay_summary: Water stress in 5 of 21 years, crop failure risk in 2 (2012, 2023).

why: This is the rotation you use today, shown as the baseline.

evidence.claim: The field is bare during May, one of the two heaviest-rain months.
In 2012 the corn year would have hit severe water stress.

benefits: Familiar to you, no new equipment
data_gaps: Your real yields per year are not known. Add them to the Farm Journal.
risks_for_local_review: Soil erosion on the east slope during bare spring months

rotations.name: Corn - Soybean + cereal rye cover crop
rotations.replay_summary: Water stress in 6 of 21 years, crop failure risk in 2 (2012, 2023).

why: Your field is bare for 7 months, including heavy-rain May. A winter cover crop keeps the soil covered.

evidence.claim: The east side of the field has slopes up to 6.5%.

data_gaps: Cover crop water use in spring is estimated, not measured.
risks_for_local_review: Rye uses spring water. In dry springs, terminate it early before planting corn.

rotations.name: Corn - Soybean - Wheat + red clover
rotations.replay_summary: Water stress in 3 of 21 years, no crop failure years.

why: Wheat finishes in July, before the driest part of summer, so it avoids most drought stress.
Clover adds nitrogen for next year's corn.

evidence.claim: July has the biggest water deficit of the year.
In 2012 the wheat year would have had moderate stress instead of failure.

data_gaps: Local wheat prices and buyers are not known.
risks_for_local_review: Wheat disease risk (head scab) in wet springs
Check there is a local market for wheat
